fresco.ApiTokenManagement.aPITokenCreate.description: Title of the success dialog shown after an API token has been created; the dialog displays the new token one time.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.areYouSureYouW.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to delete this API token? Any applications using this token will no longer be able to authenticate.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.copiedToClipbo.description: Title of the success toast shown after the researcher copies the newly created API token to the clipboard. A statement of what happened.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.copyCreateToke.description: Confirm button of the Create API Token dialog in Settings; pressing it creates the API token. A verb phrase.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.copyDeleteToke.description: Confirm button of the Delete API Token dialog in Settings; pressing it permanently deletes the API token. A verb phrase.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.copyDeleting.description: Label of the confirm button of the Delete API Token dialog while the token is being deleted. Replaces Delete Token for a moment.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.copyNever.description: Shown in the Last Used cell of the API tokens table in Settings when the token has never been used to make a request.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.copyToClipboar.description: Button in the API Token Created dialog that copies the new API token to the clipboard. A verb phrase.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.createANewAPIT.defaultMessage: Create a new API token for authenticating Interview Data API requests.
fresco.ApiTokenManagement.createANewAPIT.description: Explanatory text under the title of the Create API Token dialog. Interview Data API is the name of the Fresco feature that lets programs fetch interview data.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.createAPIToken.description: Title of the dialog in Settings where the researcher creates a new API token. API tokens authorise programs to read interview data.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.createNewToken.description: Button above the API tokens table in Settings that opens the dialog for creating a new API token.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.created.description: Column heading in the API tokens table in Settings above when each token was created. A noun phrase, not a status.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.deleteAPIToken.description: Title of the dialog that asks the researcher to confirm deleting an API token in Settings.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.description.description: Column heading in the API tokens table in Settings above the text the researcher gave each token to remember what it is for. A noun.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.descriptionOpt.description: Label of the text field in the Create API Token dialog for a note about what the token is for. The field may be left empty.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.eGDevelopmentT.description: Placeholder example shown in the empty description field of the Create API Token dialog; it suggests a possible description and is not kept.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.lastUsed.description: Column heading in the API tokens table in Settings above when each token last made a request.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.noAPITokensCre.description: Message shown in place of the rows of the API tokens table in Settings when no API token exists yet.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.status.description: Column heading in the API tokens table in Settings above the switch that turns each token on or off.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.tableLabel.description: Accessible name of the table listing API tokens, announced by screen readers when it is reached.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.untitled.description: Shown in italics in the Description cell of the API tokens table for a token created without a description. Also used in the accessible name of its switch.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.yourAPIToken.description: Heading of the highlighted box in the API Token Created dialog, above the newly created API token text.

fresco.ApiTokenManagement.yourTokenHasBe.defaultMessage: Your token has been created and is displayed below. Save this token somewhere safe now - you won't be able to see it again after you close this dialog.
fresco.ApiTokenManagement.yourTokenHasBe.description: Explanatory text under the title of the API Token Created dialog, warning that the displayed API token cannot be shown again after the dialog is closed.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.copyYourEx.description: Body of the success toast shown after an interview data export file has downloaded and every selected interview was included.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.copyYourEx.defaultMessage: Your export has downloaded. {value1, plural, one {# interview could not be exported.} other {# interviews could not be exported.}}

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.exportCanc.description: Title of the toast shown after the researcher cancelled an interview data export that was in progress. Export is a noun.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.exportComp.description: Title of the success toast shown when an interview data export has finished and its file has downloaded. Export is a noun.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.exportDown.description: Title of the toast shown when an interview data export file downloaded but the interviews could not be marked as exported afterwards. Export is a noun.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.exportErro.defaultMessage: The export could not be completed. Please try again.
fresco.ExportProgressProvider.exportErro.description: Body of the persistent error toast shown when exporting interview data failed for a reason other than cancelling.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.exportFail.description: Title of the persistent error toast shown when an interview data export failed. Export is a noun.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.exportingI.description: Title of the progress toast shown while interview data is being prepared for export; the toast has a progress bar and a cancel button.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.theExportW.description: Body of the toast shown after the researcher cancelled an interview data export; no file is downloaded.

fresco.ExportProgressProvider.yourExport.defaultMessage: Your export downloaded, but its status could not be updated. Refresh to see the latest.
fresco.ExportProgressProvider.yourExport.description: Body of the toast shown when the export file downloaded but the exported status of the interviews could not be saved. Refresh means reload the page.

fresco.ImportToastContent.complete.description: Title of the protocol import toast when a protocol file has been imported successfully.

fresco.ImportToastContent.duplicates.description: Progress step shown in the protocol import toast while Fresco checks whether the same protocol or media files were already imported.

fresco.ImportToastContent.extracting.description: Progress step shown in the protocol import toast while the media files are unpacked from the protocol file.

fresco.ImportToastContent.failed.description: Title of the protocol import toast when importing a protocol file has failed; the error and a retry button appear under it.

fresco.ImportToastContent.parsing.description: First progress step shown in the protocol import toast while the chosen protocol file is opened and read.

fresco.ImportToastContent.saving.description: Progress step shown in the protocol import toast while the imported protocol is being saved to the database.

fresco.ImportToastContent.uploadingAsset.description: Progress step shown in the protocol import toast while the protocol's media files (images, audio, video) are uploaded to storage.

fresco.ImportToastContent.uploadingProto.description: Progress step shown in the protocol import toast while the protocol file itself is uploaded to storage.

fresco.ImportToastContent.validating.description: Progress step shown in the protocol import toast while the protocol is checked for errors.

fresco.InterviewsTable.ActionsDropdown.a.description: Label at the top of the actions menu of an interviews table row, above the delete, export and enter-interview items.

fresco.InterviewsTable.ActionsDropdown.e.description: Menu item in the actions menu of an interviews table row that opens that interview in the interview screen, as the participant would see it.
Menu item in the actions menu of an interviews table row that opens the dialog for exporting that one interview's data. Export is a verb.

fresco.InterviewsTable.ActionsDropdown.o.description: Accessible name of the icon button at the end of an interviews table row that opens the row's actions menu; read only by screen readers.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.complete.description: Preset option in the Progress filter of the interviews table that selects interviews at 100% progress (finished). An adjective for the interview, not an action.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.edges.description: Option in the entity type dropdown of the Network filter of the interviews table. value is an edge type name defined by the protocol author; keep it as is.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.entityTyp.description: Label of the first dropdown in the Network filter of the interviews table, where the researcher picks which type of node or edge to count. Entity means a node or an edge.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.exportSta.description: Column heading of the interviews table for whether and when each interview's data was last exported. Also the label of its filter.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.exported.description: Option in the Export Status filter of the interviews table that selects interviews whose data has already been exported. Status, not an action.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.inProgres.description: Preset option in the Progress filter of the interviews table that selects interviews between 1% and 99% progress (begun but not finished).

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.network.description: Column heading of the interviews table for the summary of the network (people or things and their connections) recorded in each interview.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.nodes.description: Option in the entity type dropdown of the Network filter of the interviews table. value is a node type name defined by the protocol author; keep it as is.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.notExport.description: Option in the Export Status filter of the interviews table that selects interviews whose data has never been exported. Status, not an action.
Red badge in a cell of the Export Status column of the interviews table when the interview's data has never been exported.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.notStarte.description: Preset option in the Progress filter of the interviews table that selects interviews with 0% progress (no stage reached yet).

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.participa.description: Alternative text of the small participant icon shown beside the Participant Identifier column heading of the interviews table; read only by screen readers.
Column heading of the interviews table for the study participant's identifier, the label that identifies the participant who took the interview.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.progress.description: Column heading of the interviews table for how far through its stages each interview has got, shown as a bar and a percentage. Also the label of its filter.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.protocolI.description: Alternative text of the small protocol icon shown beside the Protocol Name column heading of the interviews table; read only by screen readers.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.protocolN.description: Column heading of the interviews table for the name of the interview protocol each interview was conducted with. Also the label of its filter.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.selectRow.description: Accessible name of the checkbox at the start of each row of the interviews table; read only by screen readers. Selects that one interview.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.started.description: Column heading of the interviews table for the time the interview was started. Past participle used as a label, not an action.

fresco.InterviewsTable.Columns.updated.description: Column heading of the interviews table for the time the interview was last changed. Past participle used as a label, not an action.

fresco.InterviewsTable.InterviewsSelecti.description: Button in the floating selection bar of the Interviews table; starts deleting the selected interviews (trash icon, destructive colour).
Accessible name of the close (X) button in the selection bar of the Interviews table; clears the selection. Read only by screen readers.
Button in the floating selection bar of the Interviews table; starts exporting the interview data of the selected interviews (verb, not a noun).

Text button in the floating selection bar of the Interviews table, shown when only some rows are selected; selects every interview matching the current filters. value1 is the total number of interviews.
Count of selected rows, shown in the floating bar at the bottom of the Interviews table once rows are selected. value1 is the number of selected interviews.

fresco.InterviewsTable.InterviewsTable.e.description: Title of the error toast on the Interviews page, shown above the error text when the interviews to select, export or delete could not be loaded.

Menu item in the export menu of the Interviews page. Starts an export of the data of every interview matching the current filters, finished or not.
Menu item in the export menu of the Interviews page. Starts an export of the data of only the interviews matching the current filters that have not been exported before.
Label of the button above the Interviews table that opens a menu of choices for exporting interview data (a verb phrase, not a heading).

fresco.InterviewsTable.InterviewsTable.f.description: Placeholder of the search box above the Interviews table. The researcher types a participant identifier to narrow the list of interviews.

fresco.InterviewsTable.InterviewsTableRo.description: Accessible name of the table listing interviews, announced by screen readers when it is reached.

fresco.InterviewsTable.NetworkSummary.no.description: Shown in the network column of a row of the Interviews table when the interview has recorded no nodes (people or other entities) and no edges (relationships) yet.

fresco.MobileNavDrawer.closeNavigationMe.description: Accessible name of the X button at the top of the mobile navigation menu that closes it. Read only by screen readers.

fresco.MobileNavDrawer.interviews.description: Link in the mobile navigation menu of the dashboard that opens the Interviews page, where the researcher sees and exports recorded interviews.

fresco.MobileNavDrawer.mobileNavigation.description: Accessible name of the slide-out navigation menu shown on small screens and of the navigation landmark inside it. Read only by screen readers.

fresco.NavigationBar.participants.description: Link in the main navigation bar of the researcher dashboard that opens the page listing study participants.

fresco.NavigationBar.protocols.description: Link in the main navigation bar of the researcher dashboard that opens the page listing the uploaded interview protocols.

fresco.NavigationBar.settings.description: Link in the main navigation bar of the researcher dashboard that opens the installation settings page. Noun, not the verb.

fresco.OnboardSteps.CreateAccount.create.description: Heading of the account step of the first-time setup wizard, above the form that creates the installation's first researcher account.

fresco.OnboardSteps.Documentation.thisIs.description: Paragraph under the heading of the last setup wizard step. Says setup is finished and points to the two documentation links shown below it.

fresco.OnboardSteps.Documentation.usingF.description: Small heading of a link card in the last setup step; the card links to the documentation guide on how to use Fresco.

fresco.OnboardSteps.Documentation.usingF.description: Accessible name of the "Using Fresco" documentation link card in the last setup step; read only by screen readers. Says the link opens a usage guide in a new browser tab.

fresco.OnboardSteps.Documentation.visitO.defaultMessage: Visit our documentation site to learn more about Fresco.
fresco.OnboardSteps.Documentation.visitO.description: Description text in the "About Fresco" link card of the last setup step, inviting the researcher to open the documentation site.

fresco.ParticipantsTable.Columns.uniqueP.description: Column heading in the participants table above the buttons that generate or copy each participant's personal interview link (URL).

fresco.ParticipantsTable.ParticipantsSel.description: Button in the floating selection bar of the Participants table that deletes the selected participants, after a confirmation dialog.

fresco.ProtocolsTable.ActionsDropdown.op.description: Accessible name of the icon-only button at the end of each row of the protocols table that opens that protocol's actions menu; read only by screen readers.

fresco.ProtocolsTable.AnonymousRecruitme.defaultMessage: Failed to copy URL to clipboard.

fresco.RecoveryCodes.copySaveTheseCodesI.defaultMessage: Save these codes in a safe place.

fresco.VersionSection.ofFrescoIsAvailabl.description: Title of the blue alert under the App Version setting announcing a newer Fresco release. value1 is the new version number, such as 4.2.0. Keep Fresco as the product name.

fresco.VersionSection.thisUpdateIsAMajor.defaultMessage: This update is a major version bump. A new major version may change the interview experience, or require additional configuration before the app can continue to be used. It should NOT be done while collecting data. If you are actively collecting data, please wait until data collection is complete before updating.
fresco.VersionSection.thisUpdateIsAMajor.description: Body of the Major update warning under the App Version setting. Warns that a new major version may change the interview experience and should not be installed while collecting data.

fresco.VersionSection.toUpgradeYourFresc.defaultMessage: To upgrade your Fresco version, you will need to sync your fork with the latest version of the Fresco repository. For more information, please refer to the <tag1> upgrade documentation. </tag1>
fresco.VersionSection.toUpgradeYourFresc.description: Instructions in the new-version alert under the App Version setting for upgrading the installation. The tag1 element is a link to the upgrade documentation, opened in a new tab; keep the tags around the link text.

fresco.VersionSection.viewFullReleaseNot.description: Button at the bottom of the new-version alert under the App Version setting that opens the full release notes of the new Fresco release on GitHub in a new tab.

fresco.VersionSection.youAreCurrentlyRun.description: Description under the App Version setting in Settings. value1 is the version number such as 4.1.2; value2 is the short build identifier (a commit hash), or "ci-build". Keep Fresco as the product name.

fresco.VersionSection.youAreRunningTheLa.defaultMessage: You are running the latest version of Fresco.
fresco.VersionSection.youAreRunningTheLa.description: Body of the green alert under the App Version setting, below the "You are up to date" title, confirming the newest Fresco release is installed. Keep Fresco as the product name.

fresco.VersionSection.youAreUpToDate.description: Title of the green alert under the App Version setting shown when the installation already runs the newest Fresco release.

fresco.actions.apiTokens.copyFailedToCre.description: Error toast shown in the API tokens section of Settings when creating a new API token (a credential for programmatic access to this installation) failed.

fresco.actions.apiTokens.copyFailedToDel.description: Error toast shown in the API tokens section of Settings when deleting an API token failed.

fresco.actions.apiTokens.copyFailedToUpd.description: Error toast shown in the API tokens section of Settings when switching an API token between active and inactive failed.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyCannotSet.defaultMessage: Cannot set app setting to null
fresco.actions.appSettings.copyCannotSet.description: Internal error raised when saving an installation setting is attempted with an empty (null) value. Rarely seen; reported inside the generic failure to save a setting.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyCannotSet.defaultMessage: Cannot set app setting to undefined
fresco.actions.appSettings.copyCannotSet.description: Internal error raised when saving an installation setting is attempted with no value at all (undefined). Rarely seen; reported inside the generic failure to save a setting.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyFailedToU.description: Error shown when saving a change to an installation setting in the dashboard or setup wizard fails for any reason.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyInvalidAp.description: Error shown when a researcher's attempt to change an installation setting names a setting that does not exist. value1 is the internal name of that setting.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyInvalidVa.description: Internal error raised when the value a researcher entered for an installation setting is not acceptable for that setting. value1 is the internal name of the setting.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyStorageIs.defaultMessage: Storage is configured via environment variables and cannot be changed here.
fresco.actions.appSettings.copyStorageIs.description: Error shown when a researcher tries to change a file storage setting (S3 or UploadThing) that the server administrator fixed through environment variables, so it cannot be edited in the dashboard.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyTheUpload.defaultMessage: The UploadThing token is configured via the UPLOADTHING_TOKEN environment variable and cannot be changed here.
fresco.actions.appSettings.copyTheUpload.description: Validation error under the UploadThing token field when the server administrator already set the token through an environment variable, so it cannot be edited in the app. UPLOADTHING_TOKEN is the variable name; keep it.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyTokenIsMi.defaultMessage: Token is missing required fields (apiKey, appId).
fresco.actions.appSettings.copyTokenIsMi.description: Validation error under the UploadThing token field when the pasted token decodes but lacks the apiKey or appId values it must contain. apiKey and appId are technical names; keep them.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyTokenIsNo.defaultMessage: Token is not valid. Make sure you copied the full token.
fresco.actions.appSettings.copyTokenIsNo.description: Validation error under the UploadThing token field when the pasted text cannot be read as a token, usually because it was copied incompletely.

fresco.actions.appSettings.copyTokenVeri.defaultMessage: Token verification failed. Check the token and try again.
fresco.actions.appSettings.copyTokenVeri.description: Validation error under the UploadThing token field when UploadThing rejected the token on a test request, so the token is wrong or revoked.

fresco.actions.auth.copyIncorrectUsernam.description: Error shown above the sign-in form when the username does not exist or the password is wrong. Deliberately does not say which.

fresco.actions.auth.copyInvalidFormSubmi.description: Error shown in the first-account form of the setup wizard when the server rejects the submitted username or password as invalid.

fresco.actions.auth.copyInvalidUsernameO.description: Error shown above the recovery-code sign-in form when the username does not exist or the two-factor recovery code is wrong or already used.

fresco.actions.auth.copyServerConfigurat.defaultMessage: Server configuration error. Please contact an admin.
fresco.actions.auth.copyServerConfigurat.description: Error shown above the sign-in form when the password was right but two-factor sign-in cannot continue because the installation has no installation ID. The administrator must fix the server.

fresco.actions.auth.copySetupIsAlreadyCo.description: Error shown in the first-account form of the setup wizard when someone submits it after the installation has already been set up.

fresco.actions.auth.copyTooManyAttemptsP.defaultMessage: Too many attempts. Please try again later.
fresco.actions.auth.copyTooManyAttemptsP.description: Error shown above the recovery-code sign-in form when too many sign-in attempts were made recently and the researcher is temporarily blocked.

fresco.actions.auth.copyUnauthorized.description: Error returned when a researcher tries to sign out but there is no signed-in session, for example because it already expired.

fresco.actions.auth.copyUsernameAlreadyT.description: Error shown in the first-account form of the setup wizard when the chosen username could not be saved, because it is already used.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyAnonymousP.description: Label stored on the participant record created automatically when someone starts an interview without a participant identifier. The researcher sees it in the participants list and interview table.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyAnonymousR.description: Error returned when an interview link carries no participant identifier but the installation does not allow anonymous recruitment. Recorded internally; the participant sees a separate page explaining this.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyFailedToCo.description: Error returned when marking interviews as exported fails after their data export has been downloaded. The researcher is not shown this wording; it is only the internal error text.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyFailedToCr.description: Error returned when an interview could not be created because of an unexpected failure. Recorded internally; the participant who opened the link sees a generic error page.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyFailedToDe.description: Error returned when deleting the selected interviews from the database fails. The delete confirmation dialog on the Interviews page does not currently display it.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyFailedToLo.description: Error shown in a toast when the unfinished interviews of a protocol could not be loaded while generating their interview links for export.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyFailedToRe.description: Error shown in a toast on the Interviews page when the list of interviews matching the current filter, or the details of the selected interviews, could not be loaded before an export, selection or deletion.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyInvalidPar.description: Error returned when an interview cannot be started because the participant identifier in the interview link is not valid (for example too long or only whitespace). Recorded internally; the participant sees a generic error page.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyProtocolCo.defaultMessage: This protocol could not be read, so interviews cannot be started with it.
fresco.actions.interviews.copyProtocolCo.description: Error returned when an interview cannot be started because the stored protocol (its stages, codebook or experiments) is damaged and cannot be read. Recorded internally; the participant sees a generic error page.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyProtocolIs.defaultMessage: Protocol is stored under a schema version this deployment cannot run. Repair it in Architect and upload it again.
fresco.actions.interviews.copyProtocolIs.description: Error returned when an interview cannot be started because the stored protocol uses a schema version this installation cannot run. Architect is the protocol design app. Recorded internally; the participant sees a generic error page.

fresco.actions.interviews.copyProtocolNo.description: Error returned when an interview cannot be started because the protocol no longer exists. Triggered by a participant opening an interview link; used internally, the participant sees a separate invalid-link page.

fresco.actions.participants.copyFailedTo.description: Error shown to the researcher when adding participants, one by one or by CSV import, fails on the server.
Error returned to the Participants page when looking up the selected participants fails, for example when preparing to export or delete them.
Error shown to the researcher when saving edits to an existing participant's identifier or label fails on the server.

fresco.actions.protocols.copyFailedToCle.defaultMessage: Failed to clean up uploaded files
fresco.actions.protocols.copyFailedToCle.description: Error message returned when removing the files already uploaded to storage failed, after a protocol import was abandoned. The import has already failed; this concerns the leftover files.

fresco.actions.protocols.copyFailedToDel.description: Error message returned by the server action that deletes protocols from the Protocols page, when deleting the selected protocols failed.

fresco.actions.protocols.copyTheProtocol.defaultMessage: The protocol you attempted to add already exists in the database. Please remove it and try again.
fresco.actions.protocols.copyTheProtocol.description: Error shown in the protocol import progress toast when the researcher imports a protocol file whose protocol is already installed. Tells them to delete the existing protocol first.

fresco.actions.protocols.copyThereWasAnE.defaultMessage: There was an error adding your protocol to the database. See the error details for more information.
fresco.actions.protocols.copyThereWasAnE.description: Error shown in the protocol import progress toast when saving the imported protocol to the database failed for a reason other than it already existing.

fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyCanno.defaultMessage: Cannot change storage configuration after protocols have been uploaded.
fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyCanno.description: Error shown in the S3 storage form when the researcher saves new S3 settings after interview protocols have already been uploaded to the current storage.

fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyCanno.defaultMessage: Cannot change storage provider after protocols have been uploaded.
fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyCanno.description: Error shown when the researcher tries to switch storage provider (S3 or UploadThing) after interview protocols have already been uploaded, because those files live in the current storage.

fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyCould.defaultMessage: Could not connect to the S3 bucket. Check the endpoint, bucket name, and credentials.
fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyCould.description: Error shown in the S3 storage form when saving settings and the connection test against the S3-compatible bucket fails. The endpoint is the storage service address; credentials are the access key ID and secret.

fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyS3Sto.defaultMessage: S3 storage is configured via environment variables and cannot be changed here.
fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyS3Sto.description: Error shown in the S3 storage form when the researcher saves S3 settings but the installation already supplies them through environment variables.

fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyTheSt.defaultMessage: The storage provider is configured via the STORAGE_PROVIDER environment variable and cannot be changed here.
fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyTheSt.description: Error shown in the setup wizard storage step when the researcher picks a storage provider (S3 or UploadThing) but the installation fixes it through an environment variable. Keep STORAGE_PROVIDER as written.

fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyTheSt.defaultMessage: The storage provider is pinned to UploadThing via the STORAGE_PROVIDER environment variable.
fresco.actions.storageProvider.copyTheSt.description: Error shown in the S3 storage form when the researcher saves S3 settings but an environment variable fixes the storage provider to UploadThing. Keep STORAGE_PROVIDER as written.

fresco.actions.syntheticinterviews.copyF.description: Error returned when the researcher asked to delete all generated test (synthetic) interviews and participants in Settings and the deletion failed.

fresco.actions.totp.copyCannotResetYourO.defaultMessage: Cannot reset your own two-factor authentication
fresco.actions.totp.copyCannotResetYourO.description: Error returned when a researcher tries to reset two-factor authentication on their own account; resetting is only allowed for another researcher's account.

fresco.actions.totp.copyFresco.description: Issuer name shown in the authenticator app next to the researcher's account when they scan the two-factor QR code. value is the hostname of this installation. Keep Fresco as the product name.

fresco.actions.totp.copyInvalidCode.description: Error returned when the two-factor code submitted while setting up, disabling or regenerating recovery codes is not in the expected form, such as not six digits.

fresco.actions.totp.copyInvalidCodeForma.description: Error returned when the code entered is neither a six-digit authenticator code nor a recovery code, so it cannot be checked.

fresco.actions.totp.copyInvalidRecoveryC.description: Error returned when the two-factor recovery code (a single-use backup code) the researcher entered does not exist or was already used.

fresco.actions.totp.copyInvalidVerificat.description: Error returned when the six-digit code from the researcher's authenticator app is wrong, in the two-factor setup, disable, recovery-code or re-verification forms.

fresco.actions.totp.copyNoPendingTOTPSet.description: Error returned when the researcher confirms a code while setting up two-factor authentication but no setup is in progress for their account. TOTP means time-based codes from an authenticator app.

fresco.actions.totp.copyTwoFactorAuthent.description: Error returned when the researcher asks to verify, disable or regenerate recovery codes for two-factor authentication but their account has no two-factor authentication set up.

fresco.actions.totp.twoFactorRequiredByI.defaultMessage: This installation of Fresco requires two-factor authentication for every account that signs in with a password, so it cannot be turned off.
fresco.actions.totp.twoFactorRequiredByI.description: Error returned when a researcher tries to disable two-factor authentication while the REQUIRE_TWO_FACTOR environment variable is set.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyInvalidCode.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the text entered is neither a 6-digit authenticator code nor a 20-character recovery code.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyInvalidReco.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the recovery code entered is wrong or has already been used.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyInvalidSubm.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the submitted form data is malformed.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyInvalidVeri.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the 6-digit code from the authenticator app is wrong or expired.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyServerConfi.defaultMessage: Server configuration error. Please contact an admin.
fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyServerConfi.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the installation has no installation ID, so the sign-in cannot be checked. Tells the researcher to contact whoever administers the installation.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyTooManyAtte.defaultMessage: Too many attempts. Please sign in again.
fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyTooManyAtte.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the account or network address has made too many failed sign-in attempts and is temporarily rate limited.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyTwoFactorAu.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the account has no verified authenticator app set up for two-factor authentication.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyTwoFactorSe.defaultMessage: Two-factor session expired. Please sign in again.
fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyTwoFactorSe.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the short-lived token issued after the password step has expired or is invalid, so the researcher must start sign-in again.

fresco.actions.twoFactor.copyUserNotFoun.description: Error shown on the two-factor step of signing in when the researcher account named by the sign-in session no longer exists.

fresco.actions.users.copyCannotDeleteAll.defaultMessage: Cannot delete all users. At least one user must remain.
fresco.actions.users.copyCannotDeleteAll.description: Error shown in Settings, User Management, when deleting the selected researcher accounts would leave the installation with no account at all. User means researcher account.

fresco.actions.users.copyCurrentPassword.description: Error shown in the change-password dialog in Settings when the current password the researcher entered does not match their account password.

fresco.actions.users.copyFailedToCreateU.defaultMessage: Failed to create user. Username may already exist.
fresco.actions.users.copyFailedToCreateU.description: Error shown in the form for adding a researcher account in Settings, User Management, when saving the new account failed, most likely because the username is already taken.

fresco.actions.users.copyFailedToDeleteU.description: Error shown in Settings, User Management, when deleting researcher accounts failed unexpectedly. Users means researcher accounts.

fresco.actions.users.copyFailedToUpdateP.description: Error shown in the change-password dialog in Settings when saving the new password failed unexpectedly.

fresco.actions.users.copyInvalidData.description: Generic error shown in Settings, User Management, when the data sent to delete researcher accounts or to change a password is not valid. Appears as an error message in the page or in the change-password form.

fresco.actions.users.copyInvalidFormData.description: Error shown in the form for adding a researcher account in Settings, User Management, when the submitted username and password fail the server-side checks.

fresco.actions.users.copyNoValidUsersToD.description: Error shown in Settings, User Management, when deleting researcher accounts and none of the selected accounts can be deleted (a researcher cannot delete their own account).

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyAccountIsAlr.defaultMessage: Account is already in passkey mode.
fresco.actions.webauthn.copyAccountIsAlr.description: Error shown when a researcher asks to switch their account from password sign-in to passkey-only sign-in but the account already uses passkeys only.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyAccountIsAlr.defaultMessage: Account is already in password mode.
fresco.actions.webauthn.copyAccountIsAlr.description: Error shown when a researcher asks to switch their account from passkey-only sign-in to password sign-in but the account already has a password.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyAuthenticati.description: Error shown on the sign-in page when signing in with a passkey fails because the server could not verify the passkey.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyCannotRemove.defaultMessage: Cannot remove your only passkey without a password set.
fresco.actions.webauthn.copyCannotRemove.description: Error shown in the passkey list in Settings when the researcher tries to remove their last passkey while the account has no password, which would leave no way to sign in.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyCannotResetY.description: Error shown in the user accounts list in Settings when a researcher tries to reset the sign-in methods (password, passkeys, two-factor) of their own account; only another account can be reset.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyChallengeExp.description: Error shown during passkey sign-in, passkey registration or re-authentication when the short-lived passkey request (valid about 5 minutes) is missing or has expired. The researcher must start again.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyIncorrectPas.description: Error shown in the dialog for switching to passkey-only sign-in when the current password the researcher typed to confirm is wrong.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyPasskeyNotFo.description: Error shown in the passkey list in Settings when the passkey the researcher tried to remove no longer exists or belongs to another account.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyPasskeyNotRe.description: Error shown at sign-in or re-authentication when the passkey the researcher chose is not registered to this installation (or, on re-authentication, to their own account).

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyRegistration.description: Error shown when adding a new passkey (in setup, in Settings, or when switching to passkey sign-in) fails because the server could not verify the passkey the device produced.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copySetupIsAlrea.description: Error shown in the setup wizard when a researcher tries to create the first account with a passkey after the installation has already been set up.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyTooManyAttem.defaultMessage: Too many attempts. Please try again later.
fresco.actions.webauthn.copyTooManyAttem.description: Error shown on the sign-in page when passkey sign-in is temporarily blocked because too many sign-in attempts were made recently.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyUserNotFound.description: Error shown in the user accounts list in Settings when resetting another researcher account's sign-in methods fails because that account no longer exists.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyUsernameAlre.description: Error shown in the setup wizard when creating the first account with a passkey fails because the username is already used.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyUsernameMust.defaultMessage: Username must be at least 4 characters.
fresco.actions.webauthn.copyUsernameMust.description: Error shown in the setup wizard when creating the first account with a passkey and the chosen username is shorter than 4 characters.

fresco.actions.webauthn.copyVerification.description: Error shown when a signed-in researcher confirms their identity again with a passkey (re-authentication before a sensitive action) and the passkey check fails.

fresco.actions.webauthn.passkeyCannotVer.defaultMessage: This passkey cannot verify your identity. Choose a passkey that confirms who you are with a PIN, fingerprint, or face.
fresco.actions.webauthn.passkeyCannotVer.description: Error shown when adding a new passkey is refused because the device did not check the user's identity (PIN, fingerprint or face). Tells the researcher to choose a passkey that does.

fresco.actions.webauthn.passkeyDidNotVer.defaultMessage: This passkey did not verify your identity. Add a passkey that confirms who you are with a PIN, fingerprint, or face, then try again.
fresco.actions.webauthn.passkeyDidNotVer.description: Error shown when a signed-in researcher confirms their identity again with a passkey, and the device did not check their identity (PIN, fingerprint or face). Tells them to add a passkey that does.

fresco.actions.webauthn.passkeyDidNotVer.defaultMessage: This passkey did not verify your identity. Fresco requires a passkey that confirms who you are with a PIN, fingerprint, or face. Try another passkey, or ask another administrator to reset your authentication.
fresco.actions.webauthn.passkeyDidNotVer.description: Error shown on the sign-in page when a passkey is refused because the device did not check the user's identity (PIN, fingerprint or face). Suggests another passkey or asking another administrator to reset authentication.

fresco.activity.detail.accountCreatedWit.defaultMessage: User {username} created an account with a passkey ({passkey}).
fresco.activity.detail.accountCreatedWit.description: Initial account creation with a passkey. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.

fresco.activity.detail.apiTokenCreated.defaultMessage: User {username} created {descriptionMode, select, named {API token “{token}”} other {an untitled API token}}.
fresco.activity.detail.apiTokenCreated.description: API token creation; token is an optional user-authored description, never the secret. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.

fresco.activity.detail.apiTokenDeleted.description: API token deletion; token is the record identifier, never the secret. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.

fresco.activity.detail.apiTokenUpdated.description: API token update; token is the record identifier, never the secret. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.

fresco.activity.detail.authReset.description: An administrator resets another account’s authentication. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.

fresco.activity.detail.dataExported.defaultMessage: User {username} exported data for {count, plural, one {# interview} other {# interviews}}.
fresco.activity.detail.dataExported.description: A successfully committed interview export. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.

fresco.activity.detail.interviewComplete.description: A participant completed their interview; participant is their stable display value. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.

fresco.activity.detail.interviewOpened.defaultMessage: {actor, select, researcher {Interview “{interview}” was opened by user “{username}”.} other {Interview “{interview}” was opened.}}
fresco.activity.detail.interviewOpened.description: An interview is opened by a signed-in researcher or an unauthenticated participant. Preserve the interview identifier and username as literal data.

fresco.activity.detail.interviewStarted.description: A participant started an interview; participant is their stable display value. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.

fresco.activity.detail.interviewsDeleted.defaultMessage: User {username} deleted {count, plural, one {# interview} other {# interviews}}.
fresco.activity.detail.interviewsDeleted.description: Interviews deleted in one action. User-controlled values are literal data, not translated copy.
