fresco.passkeyCeremony.signInDidNotCompl.defaultMessage: Passkey sign-in did not complete. If you cancelled, try again. If your passkey cannot confirm who you are with a PIN, fingerprint, or face, use a different passkey or ask another administrator to reset your authentication.
fresco.passkeyCeremony.signInDidNotCompl.description: Error on the sign-in page when the browser closed the passkey prompt without a passkey being used: cancelled, timed out, or the passkey could not verify the person. Suggests the two ways forward.

fresco.passkeyName.device.description: Generic name for an unknown authenticator whose credential is bound to one device. Vendor and stored friendly names remain unchanged.

fresco.passkeyName.synced.description: Generic name for an unknown authenticator whose passkey is synchronized across devices. Vendor and stored friendly names remain unchanged.

fresco.protocolImport.checkAssets.defaultMessage: Could not check for existing assets.
fresco.protocolImport.checkAssets.description: Error in the protocol import toast when asking the server which of the protocol's media files (assets) are already stored fails.

fresco.protocolImport.files.unreadable.defaultMessage: The file could not be read.
fresco.protocolImport.files.unreadable.description: Error raised when the browser cannot read a protocol file the researcher chose to import (upload), so the import of that protocol file stops.

fresco.protocolImport.importedName.description: Body of the success toast after a protocol file has been imported. name is the protocol file name without the .netcanvas extension.

fresco.protocolImport.operationalFailure.defaultMessage: The protocol could not be imported. Check your connection and storage configuration, then try again.
fresco.protocolImport.operationalFailure.description: Retry guidance for lookup, storage, or persistence failures after reading a protocol; does not claim that the protocol file is invalid.

fresco.protocolImport.protocolMismatch.defaultMessage: The uploaded protocol file did not match the requested file.
fresco.protocolImport.protocolMismatch.description: Error in the protocol import toast when the file reported back by storage after upload has a different name from the protocol file the researcher chose.

fresco.protocolImport.validation.invalid.defaultMessage: The uploaded file does not contain a valid protocol.
fresco.protocolImport.validation.invalid.description: Error in the protocol import toast when the chosen file does not contain a protocol at all, for example when it is not a Network Canvas protocol file.

fresco.protocolImport.validation.missing.description: Error in the protocol import toast when upgrading an older protocol to the supported format fails because required items are absent. dependencies is a list of the missing items.

fresco.protocolImport.validation.unsuppo.defaultMessage: Protocol version not supported. Fresco supports {count, plural, one {version} other {versions}} {versions}.
fresco.protocolImport.validation.unsuppo.description: Error in the protocol import toast when the protocol's schema version is not one this Fresco can import. count is how many versions are supported; versions is the list of supported schema version numbers.

fresco.protocolImport.validation.validat.defaultMessage: The protocol is invalid. Please check the protocol structure.
fresco.protocolImport.validation.validat.description: Error in the protocol import toast when the protocol inside the imported file fails validation against the protocol format.

fresco.protocolSize.tooLarge.defaultMessage: This protocol is {size, number} MB. Protocols must be {limit, number} MB or smaller to import.
fresco.protocolSize.tooLarge.description: Error shown in a toast, titled with the file name, when a protocol file chosen for import is over the size limit. size is the file size and limit the maximum allowed, both in megabytes.

fresco.protocols.AnonymousRecruitmentWar.defaultMessage: Anonymous recruitment is enabled. This means that participants can self-enroll in your study without needing to be invited, by visiting the protocol-specific onboarding link. To disable anonymous recruitment, visit <tag1>the settings page</tag1>.
fresco.protocols.AnonymousRecruitmentWar.description: Text of the information box shown while anonymous recruitment is on: anyone with a protocol's onboarding link can start an interview without an invitation. tag1 wraps a link to the Settings page.
Title of an information box on the dashboard overview, shown only while the anonymous recruitment setting is switched on.

fresco.protocols.page.protocols.description: Main heading of the Protocols page of the dashboard, which lists the interview protocols installed on this Fresco.

fresco.protocols.page.uploadAndManageYou.defaultMessage: Upload and manage your interview protocols.
fresco.protocols.page.uploadAndManageYou.description: Sub-heading under the title of the Protocols page; says the page is for importing protocol files and managing the installed protocols.

fresco.root.metadata.pageDescription.description: Default page description (search-engine and link-preview metadata) for Fresco pages that set none of their own. Keep "Fresco" unchanged in all languages.

fresco.root.metadata.pageTitle.description: Default browser tab title for Fresco pages that set no title of their own. Keep "Network Canvas Fresco" unchanged in all languages.

fresco.settings.ApiTokensSection.aPIToke.description: Title of the card in Settings that holds the interview data API switch and the list of API tokens.

fresco.settings.ApiTokensSection.aPIToke.defaultMessage: API tokens are used to authenticate requests to the Interview Data API.
fresco.settings.ApiTokensSection.aPIToke.description: Hint under the Manage Tokens label in Settings, explaining what API tokens are for.

fresco.settings.ApiTokensSection.enableA.defaultMessage: Enable a read-only API for accessing interview data. Requires an API token for authentication.
fresco.settings.ApiTokensSection.enableA.description: Hint under the interview data API toggle in Settings. The API token is a secret that programs send to prove they may read interview data.

fresco.settings.ApiTokensSection.intervi.description: Label of the toggle in the API Tokens card of Settings that turns the read-only API for interview data on or off. Also the toggle's accessible name.

fresco.settings.ApiTokensSection.manageT.description: Label of the Settings row where the researcher creates and revokes API tokens for the interview data API. Tokens here are API tokens, not two-factor codes.

fresco.settings.ConfigurationSection.app.description: Title of the settings card that shows the installed Fresco version and the installation ID. Also the name of this section in the Settings page.

fresco.settings.ConfigurationSection.ins.description: Label of the field in Settings, App Details, that holds the unique identifier of this Fresco installation. Also its accessible name. ID is short for identifier.

fresco.settings.ConfigurationSection.thi.defaultMessage: This is the unique identifier for your installation of Fresco. This ID is used to track analytics data and for other internal purposes.
fresco.settings.ConfigurationSection.thi.description: Hint text under the Installation ID field in Settings, App Details, explaining what the identifier is used for.

fresco.settings.DeveloperToolsSection.de.defaultMessage: Delete all data and reset Fresco to its default state.
fresco.settings.DeveloperToolsSection.de.description: Warning hint under the Reset Settings label in the Developer Tools card of Settings; describes what the reset button next to it does: erases all data on this installation.
Title of the Developer Tools card in Settings, which holds the destructive reset and the recruitment test. Shown in a red, destructive style.

fresco.settings.DeveloperToolsSection.re.description: Label of the field in the Developer Tools card of Settings that holds the reset button; the hint below it explains the reset deletes everything.

fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.description: Label of the toggle in Interview Settings that allows anonymous recruitment, where study participants join through a shared link. Also the toggle's accessible name.
Label of the toggle in Interview Settings that hides the warning participants get when they open an interview on a small screen. Also the toggle's accessible name.

fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.defaultMessage: Ensure that you test your interview thoroughly on a small screen when disabling this warning. Fresco is designed to work best on larger screens, and using it on a small screen may lead to a poor user experience for participants.
fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.description: Warning alert shown in Interview Settings once the small screen warning is switched off, advising the researcher to test on small screens. Fresco is the product name.
Label of the toggle in Interview Settings that stops completed interviews from accepting further changes. Freeze means lock. Also the toggle's accessible name.

fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.defaultMessage: If anonymous recruitment is enabled, you may generate an anonymous participation URL. This URL can be shared with participants to allow them to self-enroll in your study.
fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.description: Hint under the anonymous recruitment toggle in Interview Settings, explaining that enabling it lets the researcher generate one shared link that participants use to enrol themselves.

fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.defaultMessage: If this option is enabled, the warning about using Fresco on a small screen will be disabled.
fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.description: Hint under the disable small screen warning toggle in Interview Settings. Fresco is the product name and is not translated.
Title of the card in Settings that groups options controlling how participants take interviews.
Label of the toggle in Interview Settings that limits each participant to one completed interview per protocol. Also the toggle's accessible name.

fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.defaultMessage: When enabled, completed interviews will silently reject any further data sync updates. This prevents modifications to submitted data if an interview is re-opened.
fresco.settings.InterviewSettingsSection.description: Hint under the freeze completed interviews toggle in Interview Settings. Data sync updates are the automatic saves a browser sends while an interview is open.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.added.description: Small line under a passkey's name in Settings saying when the passkey was registered. value1 is a short date, such as Nov 12, 2026.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copyAddP.description: Button in Settings that starts registering a new passkey on the researcher's account, prompting the device or browser to create one.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copyDevi.description: Status badge beside a passkey in Settings meaning the passkey exists only on one device, such as a security key, and is not synced.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copyFail.description: Error shown under the Passkeys row in Settings when the server could not begin registering a new passkey and gave no specific reason.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copyPass.description: Fallback error shown under the Passkeys row in Settings when registering a new passkey failed for a reason that has no more specific message.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copyRegi.defaultMessage: Register a passkey for the highest level of security. You will sign in without a password using biometrics or a security key.
fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copyRegi.description: Hint under the Passkeys label in Settings, shown while the researcher has no passkeys, encouraging them to register one. A security key is a physical device.
Label of the Add passkey button in Settings while the new passkey is being registered. A progress state, not a command.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copySetA.defaultMessage: Set a password before removing your only passkey
fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copySetA.description: Tooltip on the disabled Remove button of a passkey in Settings, shown when it is the account's only passkey and the account has no password.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.copySync.description: Status badge beside a passkey in Settings meaning the passkey is backed up and synced across the researcher's devices by their password manager or platform.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.lastUsed.description: Small line under a passkey's name in Settings saying when it was last used to sign in. value1 is a short date, or the word Never.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.passkeys.description: Label of the Settings row where the researcher manages the passkeys, passwordless sign-in credentials, registered on their account.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.register.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# passkey registered.} other {# passkeys registered.}}
fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.register.description: Hint under the Passkeys label in Settings, shown when the researcher has at least one passkey. count is the number of passkeys registered on the account.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.remove.description: Button that removes a passkey from the account; used on each passkey row in Settings and as the confirm button of the removal dialog. The passkey can no longer be used to sign in.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.removePa.description: Title of the dialog in Settings that asks the researcher to confirm removing a passkey from their account.

fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.removeYo.defaultMessage: {nameMode, select, named {Remove "{name}"?} other {Remove this unnamed passkey?}} You won't be able to sign in with it anymore.
fresco.settings.PasskeySettings.removeYo.description: Body of the confirm dialog for removing a passkey in Settings. nameMode is named when the passkey has a name, then name is that name, otherwise unnamed.

fresco.settings.PrivacySection.disableAn.description: Label and accessible name of the toggle in the Privacy card of Settings that turns off sending anonymous usage analytics. Disable is a verb.

fresco.settings.PrivacySection.ifThisOpt.defaultMessage: If this option is enabled, no anonymous analytics data will be sent to the Network Canvas team.
fresco.settings.PrivacySection.ifThisOpt.description: Description under the Disable Analytics toggle in the Privacy card of Settings. This option refers to that toggle.

fresco.settings.PrivacySection.privacy.description: Heading of the Privacy card on the Settings page.

fresco.settings.ReadOnlyEnvAlert.thisSet.defaultMessage: This setting is controlled by your <tag1>.env</tag1> file, and so can only be changed by modifying that file.
fresco.settings.ReadOnlyEnvAlert.thisSet.description: Information banner shown in Settings above a setting that the installation fixes through its .env configuration file, so the control is disabled. The tag1 element formats the file name .env; do not translate it.

fresco.settings.SettingsNavigation.onThi.description: Heading of the side navigation on the Settings page that lists links jumping to each settings section on the page.

fresco.settings.StorageProviderSection.f.description: Hint under the Storage Provider label in Settings. value1 is the name of the storage provider in use: S3-compatible storage or UploadThing.

fresco.settings.StorageProviderSection.s.description: Title of the Storage card in Settings, where the researcher sees and edits where uploaded files are stored.

fresco.settings.StorageProviderSection.s.defaultMessage: Storage is configured via environment variables ( {value1}) and cannot be edited here. Remove these variables to manage storage from this dashboard.
fresco.settings.StorageProviderSection.s.description: Info alert in the Storage card of Settings, shown when the storage is set by server environment variables. value1 is the list of those variable names. Removing them makes storage editable here.
Label of the first field in the Storage card of Settings; names the service (S3-compatible storage or UploadThing) that stores uploaded files.

fresco.settings.StorageProviderSection.t.defaultMessage: The storage provider type cannot be changed once the application has been deployed. You can update the credentials below.
fresco.settings.StorageProviderSection.t.description: Info alert in the Storage card of Settings: the choice of storage provider is fixed after deployment, but its credentials listed below can be edited.

fresco.settings.StorageProviderSection.u.description: Label and accessible name of the field in the Storage card of Settings for the secret token that authorises Fresco to use UploadThing. Not a passkey or a two-factor code.

fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.description: Destructive button in the synthetic interview data card of Settings that deletes all generated test interviews and test participants at once. Delete is a verb.
Label of the Delete All button in the synthetic interview data card of Settings while the test interviews are being deleted. A progress state, not a command.
Button in the synthetic interview data card of Settings that creates the chosen number of generated test interviews for the selected protocol. Generate is a verb.
Label of the Generate button in the synthetic interview data card of Settings while test interviews are being created. A progress state, not a command.
Label of the Settings row with the button that deletes all generated test interviews and test participants.

fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.defaultMessage: Evaluate skip logic rules and stage network filters during generation. Stages will be skipped or see filtered nodes based on the network state at that point.
fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.description: Hint under the respect skip logic and filtering toggle in Settings. Nodes are the people or items a participant names in an interview.

fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.defaultMessage: Generate synthetic interview data for testing. Select a protocol and specify how many interviews to create.
fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.description: Hint under the Generate Test Interviews label in Settings, explaining the protocol picker and the number field beside it.
Label of the Settings row containing the protocol picker, interview count and Generate button for creating synthetic test interviews.
Title of the success toast shown when generating synthetic test interviews has finished.
Title of the error toast shown when generating synthetic test interviews failed; the toast body gives the reason.
Accessible name of the progress bar shown while synthetic test interviews are being generated; read only by screen readers.

fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.defaultMessage: {value1, number} / {value2, plural, one {# interview generated} other {# interviews generated}}
fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.description: Progress text under the generation progress bar. value1 is how many interviews have been generated so far; value2 is the total requested.
Label of the toggle in Settings that makes generated test interviews follow the protocol's skip logic and network filters. Also the toggle's accessible name.
Placeholder of the dropdown, and its accessible name, for choosing which uploaded protocol test interviews are generated for.
Label of the toggle in Settings that makes generated test interviews end early, as if participants gave up. Also the toggle's accessible name.

fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.defaultMessage: Successfully generated {value1, plural, one {# synthetic interview} other {# synthetic interviews}}.
fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.description: Body of the success toast shown after synthetic test interviews were generated. value1 is the number of interviews created.
Title of the card in Settings for generating and deleting synthetic interview data, computer-generated test interviews used to try out a protocol and exports.

fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.defaultMessage: There are currently {value1, plural, one {# synthetic interview} other {# synthetic interviews}} and {value2, plural, one {# test participant} other {# test participants}}.
fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.description: Hint under the Delete Test Interviews label in Settings. value1 is the number of synthetic interviews, value2 the number of test participants created with them.

fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.defaultMessage: When enabled, participants have an increasing chance of abandoning the interview at each stage.
fresco.settings.SyntheticInterviewDataSe.description: Hint under the simulate participant drop-out toggle in Settings. A stage is one step of an interview.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorRequirementFiel.description: Label of the read-only field that reports whether the installation requires two-factor authentication of every password account.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorRequirementFiel.defaultMessage: When the <tag1>REQUIRE_TWO_FACTOR</tag1> environment variable is set to true, every account that signs in with a password must set up two-factor authentication before it can use the dashboard, and cannot turn it off. Accounts that sign in with a passkey are not affected.
fresco.settings.TwoFactorRequirementFiel.description: Explains what the REQUIRE_TWO_FACTOR environment variable enforces and that passkey accounts are exempt. tag1 wraps the variable name in code formatting.
Accessible name of the read-only switch that shows whether the installation requires two-factor authentication.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.disabl.description: Destructive confirm button of the dialog in Settings that turns off two-factor authentication for the researcher's account. Disable is a verb.
Title of the dialog in Settings that asks the researcher to verify with a code before turning off two-factor authentication on their account.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.enterY.defaultMessage: Enter your current authenticator code or a recovery code to disable two-factor authentication.
fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.enterY.description: Description under the title of the dialog for turning off two-factor authentication. The authenticator code is the changing code from the app; the recovery code is a single-use backup code.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.enterY.defaultMessage: Enter your current authenticator code to generate new recovery codes. Your existing codes will be invalidated.
fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.enterY.description: Description under the title of the dialog for regenerating recovery codes. The authenticator code is the changing code from the app; old recovery codes stop working.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.ifYouC.defaultMessage: If you can't access your authenticator app, you need to use a recovery code to disable two-factor authentication. If you don't have any valid recovery codes, you will need another user to disable two-factor authentication for you.
fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.ifYouC.description: Info notice inside the dialog for turning off two-factor authentication, for researchers who lost their authenticator app. Another user means another researcher account on this installation.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.ifYouC.defaultMessage: If you can't access your authenticator app, you need to disable two-factor authentication using an existing recovery code before you generate new codes. If you don't have any valid recovery codes, you will need another user to disable two-factor authentication for you.
fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.ifYouC.description: Info notice inside the dialog for regenerating recovery codes, for researchers who lost their authenticator app. Another user means another researcher account on this installation.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.newRec.description: Title of the dialog in Settings that shows the newly generated two-factor recovery codes (single-use backup codes) after regeneration.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.regene.description: Confirm button of the dialog in Settings that replaces the account's recovery codes with newly created ones. Regenerate is a verb.
Label of the button in Settings, and title of the dialog it opens, for replacing the account's two-factor recovery codes (single-use backup codes) with new ones.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.requir.defaultMessage: Two-factor authentication is required on this installation for every account that signs in with a password, so it cannot be turned off here.
fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.requir.description: Shown beside the per-account two-factor switch when the REQUIRE_TWO_FACTOR environment variable is set.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.toggle.description: Accessible name of the switch in Settings that turns two-factor authentication on or off; read only by screen readers.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.twoFac.description: Label of the Settings row with the switch that turns two-factor authentication on or off for the researcher's own account.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.twoFac.defaultMessage: Two factor authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security to your account by requiring a second form of verification in addition to your password. This can be a code from an authenticator app or a recovery code.
fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.twoFac.description: Hint under the Two-Factor Authentication label in Settings. The second form of verification is a code from an authenticator app, or a recovery code.

fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.yourPr.defaultMessage: Your previous recovery codes have been invalidated. Save these new codes.
fresco.settings.TwoFactorSettings.yourPr.description: Description under the title of the dialog that shows newly generated recovery codes, telling the researcher the old codes no longer work and to keep the new ones.

fresco.settings.UpdateInstallationId.cop.description: Validation error under the installation ID field in Settings when the researcher clears the field and tries to save an empty value.

fresco.settings.UpdateS3Settings.copyFai.description: Error shown in red under an S3 storage field in Settings when saving the value the researcher entered failed.

fresco.settings.UpdateS3Settings.copySav.description: Label of the Save button under an S3 storage field in Settings while the value is being saved (progress state).

fresco.settings.UpdateS3Settings.reset.description: Button beside Save under an S3 storage field in Settings, shown after the text was changed; puts the field back to its last saved value (verb).

fresco.settings.UpdateUploadThingToken.s.description: Placeholder of the empty UploadThing API token field in Settings; the dots stand for the saved token, which is never shown. Keep the dots.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.actions.description: Column heading of the users table in Settings for the row buttons (reset authentication, delete).

fresco.settings.UserManagement.addUser.description: Button above the users table in Settings and title of the dialog it opens; creates a new researcher account (verb).

fresco.settings.UserManagement.allUsers.description: Heading above the users table in Settings, also its accessible name; the table lists the researcher accounts of this installation.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.allYourPa.defaultMessage: All your passkeys will be removed and replaced with a password.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.allYourPa.description: Description under the title of the Switch to Password Authentication dialog in Settings; warns that every passkey of the account is removed.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.areYouSur.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to delete the user "{value1}"? This action cannot be undone.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.areYouSur.description: Body of the confirmation dialog opened by the Delete button in a row of the users table in Settings. value1 is the username of that researcher account.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.atLeast4C.description: Hint listing the rules for the username field of the Add User dialog in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.atLeast8C.defaultMessage: At least 8 characters with lowercase, uppercase, number, and symbol
fresco.settings.UserManagement.atLeast8C.description: Hint under a new-password field (Add User, Change Password and Switch to Password dialogs in Settings) stating the password rules.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.authMetho.description: Column heading of the users table in Settings; the column says how each researcher account signs in (password, password with two-factor, or passkey).

fresco.settings.UserManagement.changePas.description: Button in the account section of Settings that opens the dialog for changing the researcher's own password, and the title of that dialog (verb).

fresco.settings.UserManagement.confirmNe.description: Label of the field in which the new password is typed a second time, in the Change Password and Switch to Password Authentication dialogs in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.confirmPa.description: Label of the field in which the password is typed a second time, in the Add User dialog in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyAreYo.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to delete the user "{value1}"? This action cannot be undone.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyAreYo.description: Body of the confirmation dialog for deleting the single account selected with Delete Selected in the users table in Settings. value1 is that account's username.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyAreYo.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to delete {value1, plural, one {# user} other {# users}}? This action cannot be undone.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyAreYo.description: Body of the confirmation dialog for deleting several accounts selected with Delete Selected in the users table in Settings. value1 is the number of researcher accounts.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyDelet.description: Title of the dialog that asks the researcher to confirm deleting several accounts selected with Delete Selected in the users table in Settings.
Title and confirm button of the dialog that asks the researcher to confirm deleting the single account selected with Delete Selected in the users table in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyFaile.description: Fallback form error in the Switch to Passkey Authentication dialog in Settings when the server could not prepare creating a passkey, before the browser's passkey prompt appeared.
Fallback error in the Switch to Password Authentication dialog in Settings when the server could not start the passkey identity check.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyNewPa.description: Form error shown in the Change Password dialog in Settings when the new password and its confirmation differ.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyPassk.description: Fallback form error in the Switch to Passkey Authentication dialog in Settings when creating the passkey in the browser failed and no more specific message applies.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyPassw.description: Form error shown in the Add User dialog, and in the Switch to Password Authentication dialog, in Settings, when the password and its confirmation differ.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyVerif.description: Fallback error in the Switch to Password Authentication dialog in Settings when the passkey identity check in the browser failed and no more specific message applies.
Button in the Switch to Password Authentication dialog in Settings; opens the browser's passkey prompt so the researcher proves who they are.
Label of the Verify with passkey button in the Switch to Password Authentication dialog while the passkey check is in progress.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyYouCa.defaultMessage: You cannot delete your own account
fresco.settings.UserManagement.copyYouCa.description: Error raised when the researcher uses Delete Selected in the users table in Settings and the only selected account is their own, which cannot be deleted.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.createUse.description: Submit button of the Add User dialog in Settings; creates the new researcher account (verb).

fresco.settings.UserManagement.currentPa.description: Label of the field for the researcher's existing password, in the Change Password and Switch to Passkey Authentication dialogs in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.deleteCou.description: Confirm button of the dialog opened by Delete Selected in the users table in Settings when several accounts are selected. count is the number of researcher accounts that will be deleted.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.deleteSel.description: Button in the floating bar of the users table in Settings once rows are selected; starts deleting the selected researcher accounts.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.deleteUse.description: Title and confirm button of the dialog opened by the Delete button in a row of the users table in Settings; asks to confirm deleting that researcher account.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.enterYour.defaultMessage: Enter your current password, then register a passkey. Your password and two-factor authentication will be removed.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.enterYour.description: Description under the title of the Switch to Passkey Authentication dialog in Settings; the researcher enters their password, then creates a passkey.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.loggedInA.description: Small caption above the signed-in researcher's username at the top of the account section in Settings; ends with a colon.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.mustBeUni.description: Hint for the username field of the Add User dialog in Settings: no other researcher account may have the same username.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.newPasswo.description: Label of the field for the password the researcher wants to use from now on, in the Change Password and Switch to Password Authentication dialogs in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.noUsersCr.description: Text shown in place of rows when the users table in Settings is empty.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.password.description: Label of the password field of the Add User dialog in Settings; the password of the account being created.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.passwordU.description: Success message that replaces the form of the Change Password dialog in Settings for a moment after the password was changed.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.removeAll.defaultMessage: Remove all passkeys and switch to password-based authentication.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.removeAll.description: Hint under the Switch to Password Authentication label in Settings; says all the account's passkeys are removed.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.removeYou.defaultMessage: Remove your password and two-factor authentication, and use a passkey to sign in instead.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.removeYou.description: Hint under the Switch to Passkey Authentication label in Settings; says the password and two-factor authentication are removed in favour of a passkey.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.resetAuth.description: Button in a row of the users table in Settings, for other accounts that have two-factor or passkeys, and confirm button of its dialog; removes that account's sign-in methods (verb).
Title of the dialog that asks the researcher to confirm resetting another account's authentication, opened by Reset Auth in the users table in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.securityW.description: Title of a warning alert in the account section of Settings, shown to a researcher who signs in with a password but has no two-factor authentication.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.selectAll.description: Accessible name of the checkbox in the header of the users table in Settings that selects every row; read only by screen readers.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.selectRow.description: Accessible name of the checkbox on each row of the users table in Settings that selects that researcher account; read only by screen readers.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.switchToP.description: Destructive button next to the Switch to Passkey Authentication setting in Settings, and confirm button of its dialog (verb).
Label of a setting in the account section of Settings, and title of its dialog; changes the researcher's own account from password sign-in to passkey sign-in.
Destructive button next to the Switch to Password Authentication setting in Settings, and confirm button of its dialog (verb).
Label of a setting in the account section of Settings, and title of its dialog; changes the researcher's own account from passkey sign-in to password sign-in.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.temporary.description: Title of the dialog shown after another account's authentication was reset in the users table in Settings; the dialog displays the temporary password.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.theUserSA.defaultMessage: The user's authentication has been reset. Share this temporary password with them so they can sign in and set up their account again.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.theUserSA.description: Description in the Temporary Password dialog in Settings. The user is the researcher account that was reset; the researcher reading it must pass the password on to that person.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.thisWillR.defaultMessage: This will remove all passkeys, 2FA, and recovery codes for {value1}, and set a temporary password. They will need to set up their authentication again.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.thisWillR.description: Body of the Reset Authentication confirmation dialog. value1 is the username of the researcher account being reset. 2FA is two-factor authentication; recovery codes are its backup codes.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.updatePas.description: Submit button of the Change Password dialog in Settings; saves the new password (verb).

fresco.settings.UserManagement.updateYou.description: Description under the title of the Change Password dialog in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.username.description: Column heading of the users table in Settings and label of the username field in the Add User dialog; the name a researcher signs in with.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.verifyYou.defaultMessage: Verify your identity with a passkey to continue.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.verifyYou.description: Instruction in the first step of the Switch to Password Authentication dialog in Settings, above the Verify with passkey button.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.you.description: Small marker shown after the username of the signed-in researcher's own row in the users table in Settings.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.youAreThe.defaultMessage: You are the only user. If you lose access to your passkey, you will be locked out. Consider adding another user or backing up your passkey.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.youAreThe.description: Info alert in the account section of Settings, shown to a passkey researcher when theirs is the only researcher account on the installation; warns of lockout if the passkey is lost.

fresco.settings.UserManagement.yourAccou.defaultMessage: Your account is only protected by a password. Enable two-factor authentication for stronger security.
fresco.settings.UserManagement.yourAccou.description: Body of the Security Warning alert in the account section of Settings; advises turning on two-factor authentication.

fresco.settings.UserManagementSection.us.description: Title of the Settings card that manages researcher accounts: password, passkeys, two-factor authentication and the list of users who can sign in.

fresco.settings.installationId.regenerat.description: Accessible label for the button that creates a new installation identifier.

fresco.settings.interviews.completedLimi.defaultMessage: If this option is enabled, each participant can only have one completed interview for each protocol, although they may have multiple incomplete interviews. Once an interview is completed, starting a new interview or resuming any other incomplete interview is prevented.
fresco.settings.interviews.completedLimi.description: Explains the completed-interview limit and that completion prevents both starting another interview and resuming any other incomplete interview.

fresco.settings.navigation.api.description: Name of the section in the Settings side navigation where a researcher creates and deletes API tokens, which authorise programs that read interview data from Fresco.

fresco.settings.navigation.appDetails.description: Name of the section in the Settings side navigation that shows the installed version and installation ID of Fresco.

fresco.settings.navigation.developer.description: Name of the Developer Tools section in the Settings side navigation, shown in a warning style. It holds risky tools such as deleting data and testing recruitment.

fresco.settings.navigation.interviews.description: Name of the section in the Settings side navigation for options that change how interviews run, such as limiting interviews and anonymous recruitment.

fresco.settings.navigation.privacy.description: Name of the Privacy section in the Settings side navigation, which holds privacy options such as analytics.

fresco.settings.navigation.storage.description: Name of the section in the Settings side navigation where the researcher sees where uploaded files such as protocol assets are stored.

fresco.settings.navigation.synthetic.description: Name of the section in the Settings side navigation where a researcher generates fake test interviews (synthetic data) for a protocol.

fresco.settings.navigation.users.description: Name of the section in the Settings side navigation where researcher accounts are added, removed and given sign-in methods. User means researcher, not participant.

fresco.settings.page.hereYouCanConfigure.defaultMessage: Here you can configure your installation of Fresco.
fresco.settings.page.hereYouCanConfigure.description: Subheading under the heading of the Settings page, describing the page. Fresco is the product name; installation is this researcher-hosted copy of it.

fresco.settings.page.settings.description: Heading of the Settings page of the dashboard, where the researcher configures the Fresco installation.

fresco.settings.passkeys.never.description: Shown in place of a date in the Last used line of a passkey in Settings when the passkey has never been used to sign in. Follows the words Last used.

fresco.settings.s3.accessKey.description: Label and accessible name of a password-style field in the Storage card of Settings: the identifier half of the S3 storage credentials. Not a passkey.

fresco.settings.s3.bucket.description: Label and accessible name of the text field in the Storage card of Settings for the name of the S3 bucket that holds uploaded files.

fresco.settings.s3.endpoint.description: Label and accessible name of the text field in the Storage card of Settings for the web address (URL) of the S3-compatible storage service Fresco connects to.

fresco.settings.s3.publicURL.description: Label and accessible name of the text field in the Storage card of Settings for the public web address (URL) through which the S3 bucket's files are reached.

fresco.settings.s3.region.description: Label and accessible name of the text field in the Storage card of Settings for the cloud region of the S3 storage bucket (a data-centre location, not a country setting).

fresco.settings.s3.secret.description: Label and accessible name of a password-style field in the Storage card of Settings: the secret half of the S3 storage credentials. Not a passkey or a two-factor code.

fresco.settings.storage.uploadThingHelp.defaultMessage: The API key used to communicate with UploadThing. See the <link>deployment documentation</link> for details.
fresco.settings.storage.uploadThingHelp.description: Hint under the UploadThing API key field in the Storage card of Settings. The link tag wraps the words that link to the deployment documentation; keep the tag.

fresco.settings.synthetic.countLabel.description: Accessible label for the synthetic interview count field.

fresco.settings.users.passkeyAuth.description: Value in the Auth Method column of the users table in Settings: the account signs in with a passkey (a device-based credential, not a password).

fresco.settings.users.passwordAuth.description: Value in the Auth Method column of the users table in Settings: the researcher account signs in with a password only.

fresco.settings.users.passwordTwoFactor.description: Value in the Auth Method column of the users table in Settings: the account signs in with a password plus a two-factor authentication (2FA) code.

fresco.settings.users.usernameMinimum.defaultMessage: Username must be at least 4 characters
fresco.settings.users.usernameMinimum.description: Validation error below the username field of the Add User dialog in Settings, when the username is shorter than four characters.

fresco.settings.users.usernameSpaces.description: Validation error below the username field of the Add User dialog in Settings, when the username contains a space.

fresco.settings.users.usernameTaken.description: Validation error below the username field of the Add User dialog in Settings, when another researcher account already has that username.

fresco.setup.Setup.configureStorage.description: Label of the second step in the first-run setup wizard, where the researcher chooses where uploaded files are stored (S3-compatible storage or UploadThing).

fresco.setup.Setup.createAccount.description: Label of the first step in the first-run setup wizard, where the researcher creates the installation's first account.

fresco.setup.Setup.documentation.description: Label of the last step in the first-run setup wizard, which points the researcher to the Fresco documentation. Noun, not a link.

fresco.setup.Setup.uploadProtocol.description: Label of the third step in the first-run setup wizard, where the researcher uploads an interview protocol.

fresco.signin.metadata.pageDescription.description: Meta description of the sign-in page, used by search engines and link previews. Fresco is the product name; the sentence invites the researcher to sign in.

fresco.signin.metadata.pageTitle.description: Browser tab title of the sign-in page. Fresco is the product name; Sign In is the name of the page.

fresco.signin.page.signInToFresco.description: Heading above the sign-in form on the page where a researcher signs in to the Fresco installation. It is a heading, not a button.

fresco.signin.twoFactorSetup.metadata.pa.defaultMessage: Set up two-factor authentication to continue to Fresco.
fresco.signin.twoFactorSetup.metadata.pa.description: Browser metadata description for the page that makes a researcher set up mandatory two-factor authentication after signing in.
Browser tab title for the page that makes a researcher set up mandatory two-factor authentication after signing in.

fresco.signin.twoFactorSetup.page.setItU.defaultMessage: Set it up now with an authenticator app to continue to the dashboard. You will be given recovery codes to keep somewhere safe in case you lose the app.
fresco.signin.twoFactorSetup.page.setItU.description: Tells the researcher what setting up two-factor authentication involves and that the dashboard opens once it is done.

fresco.signin.twoFactorSetup.page.setUpT.description: Heading of the page that makes a researcher set up mandatory two-factor authentication after signing in.

fresco.signin.twoFactorSetup.page.thisIn.defaultMessage: This installation of Fresco requires two-factor authentication for every account that signs in with a password.
fresco.signin.twoFactorSetup.page.thisIn.description: Explains why the researcher is being asked to set up two-factor authentication before they can reach the dashboard.

fresco.storage.s3Label.description: Label for S3 and compatible object storage providers.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.conflictSubje.defaultMessage: {entity, select, ego {Ego attributes: {variables}} node {Attributes on node type {type}: {variables}} edge {Attributes on edge type {type}: {variables}} other {Attributes: {variables}}}
fresco.syntheticGeneration.conflictSubje.description: Identifies affected codebook attributes. Type and variable names are unchanged researcher data; variables is a locale-formatted list.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.constraints.defaultMessage: Synthetic interviews could not be generated with these validation rules. Review the affected attributes below.
fresco.syntheticGeneration.constraints.description: Introduces actionable constraint conflicts reported by the shared synthetic generation engine.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.deleteFailed.defaultMessage: Could not delete synthetic data. Try again.
fresco.syntheticGeneration.deleteFailed.description: Fallback when the synthetic data deletion request fails without a specific refusal.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.interrupted.defaultMessage: Interview generation could not finish. Try again. Some interviews may already have been created.
fresco.syntheticGeneration.interrupted.description: Operational generation or stream failure; a partial batch may have been saved.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.invalidReques.defaultMessage: The interview generation request is invalid. Reload the page and try again.
fresco.syntheticGeneration.invalidReques.description: Recovery guidance for malformed generation JSON or invalid generation options.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.missingProtoc.defaultMessage: This protocol is no longer available. Select another protocol.
fresco.syntheticGeneration.missingProtoc.description: The selected protocol was not found when generation started.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.refreshFailed.defaultMessage: Could not refresh the latest data. Reload the page.
fresco.syntheticGeneration.refreshFailed.description: The generation request finished but cache invalidation failed; do not imply that saved interviews were lost.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.signInRequire.defaultMessage: Sign in to generate synthetic interviews.
fresco.syntheticGeneration.signInRequire.description: Generation request refused because there is no authenticated researcher session.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.technicalDeta.description: Disclosure label for the original, untranslated generation diagnostic.

fresco.syntheticGeneration.unreadablePro.defaultMessage: This protocol could not be read, so no interviews were generated.
fresco.syntheticGeneration.unreadablePro.description: The selected protocol's stored data does not parse, so generation was refused before creating anything.

fresco.tableFilters.NuqsClearFilterslabe.description: Button in the filter toolbar above dashboard tables (such as the activity feed) that resets all search and filter fields at once.

fresco.tableFilters.NuqsFacetedFilteremp.description: Message inside the open multi-select filter dropdown of a table, shown when the search typed in the dropdown matches no option. Default; a table can supply its own.

fresco.tableFilters.NuqsFacetedFilterpla.description: Placeholder of the closed multi-select filter dropdown above a table when no option is chosen. Default; a table can supply its own.

fresco.tableFilters.NuqsFacetedFiltersea.description: Placeholder of the search box inside the open multi-select filter dropdown of a table, which narrows the list of options. Default; a table can supply its own.

fresco.tableFilters.NuqsSearchFilterplac.description: Default placeholder of the search box above a data table (for example participants or interviews); typing narrows the rows shown. Filter is a verb.

fresco.upload.failed.description: Error raised during protocol import when uploading a protocol's asset file to storage failed because of a network problem or an unexpected failure.

fresco.upload.httpStatus.description: Error raised during protocol import when storage rejected the upload of a protocol's asset file. status is the numeric HTTP status code returned by storage.

fresco.upload.missingUrl.defaultMessage: No upload URL was returned for {name}.
fresco.upload.missingUrl.description: Error raised while uploading a protocol's asset files to storage during protocol import, when the server returned no upload address for one file. name is the file name.

fresco.upload.prepare.description: Error raised during protocol import when the server could not prepare the upload of a protocol's asset files to storage, before any file was sent.

fresco.validation.auth.validation1.defaultMessage: Username must be at least 4 characters
fresco.validation.auth.validation1.description: Validation error under the username field when creating a researcher account (setup wizard or Settings) and the username is shorter than 4 characters.

fresco.validation.auth.validation2.description: Validation error under the username field when creating a researcher account and the username contains a space character.

fresco.validation.auth.validation3.defaultMessage: Password must contain at least 1 lowercase, 1 uppercase, 1 number, and 1 symbol
fresco.validation.auth.validation3.description: Validation error under the password field when creating a researcher account and the password is too weak. A symbol means a punctuation or special character.

fresco.validation.auth.validation4.description: Validation error under the confirm-password field when creating a researcher account and it differs from the password typed above.

fresco.validation.auth.validation5.description: Validation error under the username field of the sign-in form when it is submitted empty.

fresco.validation.auth.validation6.description: Validation error under the password field of the sign-in form when it is submitted empty.

fresco.validation.participant.validation.description: Validation error under the identifier field when adding or editing a participant, and for CSV rows, when the identifier is missing or empty. The identifier is the unique ID that distinguishes a participant.

fresco.validation.participant.validation.defaultMessage: Identifier too long. Maximum of 255 characters.
fresco.validation.participant.validation.description: Validation error under the identifier field when adding or editing a participant, when a required identifier is longer than 255 characters.

fresco.validation.participant.validation.defaultMessage: Identifier requires one or more non-whitespace characters.
fresco.validation.participant.validation.description: Validation error under the identifier field when adding or editing a participant, when the identifier contains only spaces.

fresco.validation.participant.validation.defaultMessage: Identifier too long. Maximum of 255 characters.
fresco.validation.participant.validation.description: Validation error for an optional participant identifier, as in a row of an imported CSV file whose identifier is longer than 255 characters.

fresco.validation.participant.validation.defaultMessage: Label requires one or more non-whitespace characters.
fresco.validation.participant.validation.description: Validation error for a participant label when a label is required, as in a row of an imported CSV file that has no identifier, and the label is missing or only spaces. The label is an optional display name.
Error shown in the participant CSV import dialog when the chosen file is not a valid list of participants.

fresco.validation.participant.validation.defaultMessage: Invalid CSV. Every row must have either a label or an identifier
fresco.validation.participant.validation.description: Error shown in the participant CSV import dialog when at least one row of the file has neither a label nor an identifier.

fresco.validation.password.lower.defaultMessage: Password must contain at least 1 lowercase letter
fresco.validation.password.lower.description: Password strength validation rule: Password must contain at least 1 lowercase letter

fresco.validation.password.minimum.defaultMessage: Password must be at least {count, number} characters
fresco.validation.password.minimum.description: Password strength validation rule: Password must be at least {count, number} characters

fresco.validation.password.number.defaultMessage: Password must contain at least 1 number
fresco.validation.password.number.description: Password strength validation rule: Password must contain at least 1 number

fresco.validation.password.strong.defaultMessage: Password must be at least 8 characters and contain at least 1 lowercase, 1 uppercase, 1 number, and 1 symbol
fresco.validation.password.strong.description: Password strength validation rule: Password must be at least 8 characters and contain at least 1 lowercase, 1 uppercase, 1 number, and 1 symbol

fresco.validation.password.symbol.defaultMessage: Password must contain at least 1 symbol
fresco.validation.password.symbol.description: Password strength validation rule: Password must contain at least 1 symbol

fresco.validation.password.upper.defaultMessage: Password must contain at least 1 uppercase letter
fresco.validation.password.upper.description: Password strength validation rule: Password must contain at least 1 uppercase letter

fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation1.description: Validation error under the Endpoint URL field of the S3 storage form when it is left empty.

fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation2.defaultMessage: Endpoint must be a valid http(s) URL and may not target a private, loopback, or link-local address.
fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation2.description: Validation error under the Endpoint URL field of the S3 storage form when the address is not an http or https URL, or points to an internal network address (private, loopback or link-local), which is blocked for security.

fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation3.defaultMessage: Public URL must be a valid URL.
fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation3.description: Validation error under the Public URL field of the S3 storage form when the text is not a well-formed web address or is empty.

fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation4.description: Validation error under the Bucket Name field of the S3 storage form when it is left empty. A bucket is a named container for files in S3 storage.

fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation5.description: Validation error under the Region field of the S3 storage form when it is left empty. Region is the cloud data-centre region of the storage bucket.

fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation6.description: Validation error under the Access Key ID field of the S3 storage form when it is left empty. This is a storage service credential, not a passkey.

fresco.validation.s3Settings.validation7.description: Validation error under the Secret Access Key field of the S3 storage form when it is left empty. This is a storage service credential.

fresco.validation.totp.validation1.description: Error shown in the two-factor setup wizard when the code the researcher entered from their authenticator app does not have exactly six characters.

fresco.validation.totp.validation2.description: Error shown in the two-factor setup wizard when the code the researcher entered from their authenticator app contains something other than digits.

fresco.validation.totp.validation3.description: Error returned when the second sign-in step is submitted without the temporary token that links it to the first step. Token here is an internal sign-in token, not an API token or a code the researcher types.

fresco.validation.totp.validation4.description: Error shown on the two-factor sign-in step when the researcher submits without typing a two-factor code or a recovery code.

fresco.validation.totp.validation5.description: Error shown when the researcher turns off two-factor authentication without entering a code to confirm. The code is a two-factor code or a recovery code.

fresco.validation.totp.validation6.defaultMessage: Must be a 6-digit code or a recovery code
fresco.validation.totp.validation6.description: Error shown when the researcher turns off two-factor authentication and the entered text is neither a 6-digit two-factor code from the authenticator app nor a recovery code.

fresco.validation.uploadThing.minimumTok.defaultMessage: UPLOADTHING_TOKEN must have at least 10 characters.
fresco.validation.uploadThing.minimumTok.description: Validation error under the UploadThing token field, in the setup wizard and in Settings, Storage, when the pasted token is shorter than 10 characters. UPLOADTHING_TOKEN is a literal name; keep it as is.

fresco.validation.users.validation1.defaultMessage: At least one user ID is required
fresco.validation.users.validation1.description: Error returned when the researcher confirms deleting user accounts in Settings but no account was selected. User means a researcher account; ID is its internal identifier.

fresco.validation.users.validation2.description: Validation error under the current-password field of the change-password dialog in Settings when it is left empty.

fresco.validation.users.validation3.description: Validation error under the confirm-password field of the change-password dialog in Settings, when the two new passwords differ.
